summary.en: Maduro and his wife pleaded not guilty to U.S. conspiracy to torture charges. The United States lifted sanctions on Jorge Rodríguez and deployed Space Force electromagnetic and electronic warfare systems against Venezuela, echoing similar actions in Iran. A soldier who bet $400,000 on Maduro's removal made his first court appearance and was arrested by U.S. authorities. The United States may be forced to release the legal justification for recent boat strikes on drug traffickers. Two battle-related deaths were recorded in 2007, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Maduro og hans kone erklærte seg ikke skyldige i amerikanske konspirasjonsanklager om tortur. USA opphevet sanksjonene mot Jorge Rodríguez og satte i drift elektromagnetiske og elektroniske krigssystemer fra Space Force mot Venezuela, i likhet med tiltakene mot Iran. En soldat som hadde satset 400 000 dollar på at Maduro skulle bli fjernet, møtte i første omgang retten og ble arrestert av amerikanske myndigheter. USA kan bli tvunget til å offentliggjøre den juridiske begrunnelsen for de siste båtangrepene på narkotikasmuglere. To dødsfall i kamp ble registrert i 2007, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Crisis in Venezuela
background.extract: An ongoing socioeconomic and political crisis began in Venezuela during the presidencies of Hugo Chávez, Nicolás Maduro and Delcy Rodríguez. It has been marked by hyperinflation, starvation, disease, crime, and mortality rates, resulting in massive emigration. Food shortages and hyperinflation have ended, but inflation remains high. It is the worst economic crisis in Venezuela's history and considered by some sources as more severe than the Great Depression in the United States, the 1985–1994 Brazilian economic crisis, or the 2008–2009 hyperinflation in Zimbabwe. In 2019, the Institute of International Finance called it the single largest economic collapse outside of war in 45 years. Writers have compared aspects, such as unemployment and GDP contraction, to Bosnia and Herzegovina after the 1992–95 Bosnian War, and those in Russia, Cuba and Albania following the Revolutions of 1989.
